summary: Red-black tree control block with an embedded node pool (allocator, list of 0x24-byte node blocks, free list, block cursor/end, tree-header sentinel and live-node count), used for the MoLive reader / stream-segment tables.
evidence: std_RbTree_AcquireNode (0x0070C414) treats self as a 28-byte pool: *self = allocator object, +0x04 = newest 0xC-byte block header {prev, nodeCount, data}, +0x08 = free-node list (next at node+0xC), +0x0C/+0x10 = block cursor/end. std_RbTree_EraseNodeRebalance (0x0070C528) uses +0x14 as the embedded tree-header sentinel (parent +0x04, leftmost +0x08, rightmost +0x0C) and decrements the count at +0x18. 0x0010EC14 is an erase helper called with the sentinel itself, so its +0x04/+0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 byte accesses describe a tree node/header, not this control block at those offsets.

fields.name: allocator
fields.evidence: AcquireNode: piVar3 = (int*)*pool; (**(code**)*piVar3)(piVar3,0xC) allocates a block header through the allocator object's vtable slot 0, slot 2 asserts - *self is the owning allocator

fields.name: nodeBlockList
fields.evidence: AcquireNode: if (pool[1] == 0) first block; else nodeCount = *(u32*)(pool[1]+4); new block header puVar4[0]=pool[1], puVar4[1]=count, pool[1]=puVar4 - newest 0xC-byte node-block header

fields.name: freeListNode
fields.evidence: AcquireNode pops a recycled node with pool[2] = node->f_C (next at node+0xC); EraseNodeRebalance pushes it back with node->f_C = *(u32*)(tree+8); *(tree+8) = node - head of the free-node list

fields.name: nodeBlockCursor
fields.evidence: std_RbTree_AcquireNode (0x0070C414) sets pool[3] (+0xc) to node+0x24 when handing out a node and compares it with pool[4] (+0x10) to detect an exhausted block

fields.name: nodeBlockEnd
fields.evidence: std_RbTree_AcquireNode (0x0070C414) sets pool[4] (+0x10) to node + newCount*0x24 and grows a new block only when the +0xc cursor reaches it

fields.name: headerNode
fields.evidence: EraseNodeRebalance works on tree->f_14 as the intrusive tree header: header+0x04 = root, +0x08 = leftmost, +0x0C = rightmost; rotations rewrite those links - embedded _Rb_tree_header sentinel

fields.name: nodeCount
fields.evidence: EraseNodeRebalance: tree->f_18 = tree->f_18 - 1 after a node is freed; InsertNode increments *(u32*)(tree+0x18) - number of live key nodes

summary: Small-string-optimised std::string (table word, begin/end/capacity-end pointers and an 8-byte inline buffer at +0x11) used by UI window text builders.
evidence: std_String_AppendChar / std_String_PushBackByte (0x0021BC88, 0x006E4618) and the std_String FormatCtor helpers (0x006F0998 family) agree on: a table pointer at +0x00 written by every constructor, begin pointer +0x04, end pointer +0x08, capacity-end +0x0C, and the small-string buffer starting at +0x11 (asm: add r3,r0,#4; add r3,r3,#0xD; cmp end-begin,#8). So the object needs at least 0x11+8 = 0x19 bytes -> 0x1C after alignment (batch size 24 was only highest-field+width). The type name is kept as std_String because include/recovered_types.h already declares it. Sibling helpers 0x0070F2DC/0x0070F58C use the same word sequence shifted by 4 (plain begin/end/capacity buffer) and are noted in the field evidence.

fields.name: bufferEnd
